description: Team AERO-GUARD is developing a compact, non-toxic fire detection and suppression module for microgravity spacecraft and lunar habitats. Because smoke does not rise in zero-g, flames behave unpredictably near critical avionics. I am a Mechanical Engineering student at Wentworth Institute of Technology designing a wall-mounted unit that pairs active air-sampling sensors with acoustic flame deflection and ultra-fine water mist. Working solo for the 2026 challenge!
summary: AERO-GUARD is a modular, wall-mounted fire detection and suppression system engineered for microgravity spacecraft and lunar habitats. Because smoke does not rise in zero gravity, traditional ceiling detectors react too late and chemical extinguishers contaminate closed-loop life support. Guided by NASA Saffire and ACME microgravity combustion data, AERO-GUARD pairs active air-sampling sensors and edge-AI anomaly detection with targeted 40–60 Hz acoustic flame deflection and ultra-fine (<50-micron) water mist to extinguish electrical fires in under 3 seconds with zero toxic residue.
details: AERO-GUARD is a wall-mounted fire detection and suppression module engineered for microgravity spacecraft and lunar habitats. Because hot air and smoke do not rise in zero gravity, traditional ceiling detectors react too late and chemical extinguishers contaminate closed-loop life support. AERO-GUARD combines active air-sampling sensors and edge-AI combustion anomaly detection with low-frequency acoustic flame deflection (40–60 Hz) and ultra-fine water mist (<50 microns) to extinguish spacecraft fires in under 3 seconds with zero toxic residue.
dataRefs: NASA Saffire Flight Data & Microgravity Combustion Studies
